source.title: Understanding Overparametrization in Survival Models through Double-Descent
source.authors: Yin Liu; Jianwen Cai; Didong Li

page_placements.theme: Loss, accuracy and post-hoc calibration can yield different curve shapes

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps model capacity and reports test-loss curves for four deep survival models. Its results refine the general double-descent claim: the trajectory differs by model and loss, with clear, weak, or absent second descent.
record.gate_note: The reported test-loss trajectories are in Figure 2 and described in Sections 5.3–5.6. Training-loss curves are also shown and described as decreasing toward interpolation, but they do not on their own measure the claimed test-loss shape. The DeepSurv log-hazard norm comparison is a separate metric, not test error. No epoch or sample-size sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps hidden width (parameter count) for four unregularized deep survival networks on synthetic data and reports test-loss curves (Fig. 2). It argues the double-descent shape depends on the likelihood loss: clear in one model, weak in one, absent in two. Post-interpolation loss always stays above the sweet spot.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that double-descent-like behaviour in survival networks is loss-specific. PC-Hazard shows a clear second descent. DeepSurv shows a weak one that they read as an optimization stall, not true recovery. The discrete-time models show none, or at most a brief shallow dip. In every case post-interpolation test loss stays above the sweet spot, so over-parametrization is not benign for survival models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic survival data and capacity sweeps of four likelihood-based survival neural networks, rather than reproducing the original settings. It reports test-loss curves at convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed capacity trajectory differs across the four model/loss formulations: PC-Hazard shows a clear second descent, DeepSurv a weak one, and Nnet-Survival and N-MTLR none.

fits_no_version.finding: For DeepSurv, the L2 norm of the learned log-risk exceeds the true log-hazard norm. The gap grows sharply once training NPLL falls below the true NPLL (about 6.646).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In likelihood-based survival nets, driving training loss past the true-model loss inflates risk-score margins instead of improving fidelity.

fits_no_version.finding: The study proves that all four survival models admit interpolation but none admits finite-norm interpolation. It links observable double descent to loss geometry near the infimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visibility of a second descent depends on whether the loss allows near-interpolation within bounded norms (loss-geometry dependence).

record.problems: Test-loss values are presented graphically rather than as numerical values in the text. The study uses synthetic data, and the reported trajectories are aggregated across 30 replicates and summarized by the median across hyperparameter combinations; uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant test-loss rows were reported beyond the four model curves. Training-loss trajectories are described as decreasing toward interpolation but do not independently measure the claimed test-loss shape.

untested.parts: Only two-layer survival networks on one synthetic data-generating process. Other tasks, architectures and real data are not tested, and there is no quantitative check that the peak coincides with the interpolation threshold.
Non-neural model classes (random features, kernels, forests) are not tested. Only deep survival networks with different likelihood losses.
No epoch-wise test curves; losses are recorded only at convergence.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location.
No variation in label noise or regularization; all models are trained without regularization.
No re-expression of capacity as an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Training-loss curves confirming monotone decrease to the interpolation point for each model; needed to locate the threshold relative to the test-loss peak.

record.verdict_notes: Kept V4 links because the study bears on V4's claim that over-parametrized risk improves past the classical optimum, though only within deep networks. Evidence is figure-only; no numbers or uncertainty are given. All curves come from one synthetic DGP, with medians over hyperparameter grids. The introduction and Sections 5.5-5.6 differ on whether the discrete-time models show a shallow post-interpolation dip.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-capacity curves in synthetic survival settings, not deep networks generally across other tasks or settings.
No test-loss curve over training epochs is reported; models are trained to convergence.
Training sample size is not varied.
The study compares four deep survival model formulations, not a broad range of model classes beyond survival models.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
The study does not vary label noise or tune regularization to test peak dependence or disappearance.
The study does not re-express the curves using an effective parameter count to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: DeepSurv
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of model parameters and examined test loss.
rows.note: The text describes an initial decrease, a sharp rise near interpolation, then a mild downward drift that stabilizes above the first minimum; the authors characterize the recovery as weak and not a meaningful interpolating regime.
rows.check: State is right. The authors say the post-peak drift is an optimization stall from gradient saturation, not a real recovery. The curve is a median across hyperparameter combinations of a 30-replicate average, with no uncertainty reported. DeepSurv uses p = 60 versus p = 200 for the others; n is not restated but appears to be 3,500.

rows.subject: PC-Hazard
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of model parameters and examined test loss.
rows.note: The text describes test loss decreasing, rising toward the interpolation threshold, and then declining to a stable plateau. The post-interpolation plateau remains above the classical bias-variance minimum.
rows.check: Observed for the fall-rise-fall shape. The second plateau stays above the sweet-spot minimum, which matters for V4's claim that risk improves past the classical optimum. Same aggregation caveat as r1.

rows.subject: Nnet-Survival
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of model parameters and examined test loss.
rows.note: The text reports an initial decline and shallow plateau, followed by a sharp rise and eventual explosion at high capacity; it explicitly reports no secondary descent.
rows.check: Sec 5.5 says no secondary descent; test loss rises and explodes. The introduction instead describes a brief, shallow dip just after interpolation, so the text is internally inconsistent; at most a negligible dip. There is no peak-then-descent at the threshold.

source_check.problem: The absent state matches Section 5.5; the introduction inconsistently describes a brief shallow post-interpolation dip.
